definition: Reasoning that unfolds across several exchanges with a user or an environment rather than in one response, which both sources identify as an under-measured regime. One builds a benchmark for it — 4 classes, 40 tasks, 3600 instances, fully automated construction and evaluation — and finds even cutting-edge reasoning models fall short. The other uses multi-turn reasoning as one of two attempted remedies for the finding that fewer than 25% of reasoning traces follow a given instruction. The archive is otherwise dominated by single-turn math and QA, so this pair marks a gap rather than filling it.

evidence.note: A fully automated multi-turn reasoning benchmark of 40 tasks and 3600 instances requiring interaction with an environment, on which frontier reasoning models fall short.
evidence.title: MTR-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multi-Turn Reasoning Evaluation

evidence.note: Benchmarks whether reasoning models follow instructions inside their reasoning traces, finding under 25% compliance at best and worse as difficulty rises.
evidence.title: ReasonIF: Large Reasoning Models Fail to Follow Instructions During Reasoning

name: multi-turn reasoning
